clue.text: Possible clue to tablet found in war zone

indicators.note: says the answer, read as a clue itself, would lead a solver to the next word

parts.note: its letters are the six letters of the first part rearranged, with the second part read as the signal to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tablet, perhaps an inscribed stone, unearthed amid the ruins of a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a clue: BATTLE with GROUND (as in ground up, broken) as the anagram signal gives TABLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleground is the site of fighting, a place where armies meet.

clue.text: Little Elizabeth describes surprising urge to get pot?

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the name goes around the other letters

parts.note: Bet is a short form of the name Elizabeth

indicators.note: a surprising version of the word is an unexpected rearrangement of it

explanation.surface: A woman called Bet has a sudden craving that leads to a paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describes' is used in its geometric sense, as a compass describes a circle: the name is drawn round the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot, or potbelly, is a protruding stomach, which a heavy drinker's paunch is.

clue.text: Key contact in Catalonia

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of the place name

explanation.surface: A key person to get in touch with in the Spanish region of Catalonia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key contact' looks like a useful person; in locksmithing the talon is the part of a bolt that the key pushes against.
explanation.definitionFit: The talon of a lock bolt is the shoulder that the turning key bears on to move it.

clue.text: Every so often learns coarse theory in University

indicators.note: taking a letter, then skipping one, all along the three words

explanation.surface: A student occasionally picks up some crude theory while at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is a British university, in the city of that name in north-west England.

clue.text: Ghastly smut, mostly

indicators.note: means most of the word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: smut is soot or dirt, which is grime

explanation.surface: Smutty material is mostly appalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim and ghastly are synonyms for something dreadful or horrible.

clue.text: Maybe Lynn was in debt to guards, becoming intimidated

indicators.note: the debt word surrounds and protects the singer's first name

parts.note: to have owed is to have been in debt
Vera Lynn was the wartime singer; 'maybe' marks her as one example of a Lynn

explanation.surface: Perhaps Vera Lynn owed money to prison guards and came to be frightened of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Vera Lynn was the British singer famed for 'We'll Meet Again' in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overawed is to be cowed or daunted by something impressive, so intimidated.

clue.text: I run after half-cut Dorries, which is a low point

indicators.note: half of her first name is cut away, leaving its first three letters

parts.note: Nadine Dorries is a former Conservative MP and culture secretary
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone runs after a drunk former minister, which is a low moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it trims Nadine to NAD; 'after' puts I and R behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of something, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: I'm eating nuts in stall

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to eating nuts while standing at a market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain time is to delay deliberately so as to get more time, which is stalling.

clue.text: Risks going topless in French city

indicators.note: the word loses its top, which in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: risks are dangers

explanation.surface: The hazards of sunbathing topless in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Angers is a city in the Loire valley in western France.

clue.text: Doctor leaves aubergine in back of practice for Rose

indicators.note: the doctor departs from the vegetable word, so those letters are removed

parts.note: eggplant is the American name for the aubergine
GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A doctor abandons a vegetable at the rear of the surgery and picks up a rose instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Rose' disguises a flower as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild species of rose.

clue.text: Rewrite 6 Down

indicators.note: to rewrite the word is to set its letters down in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 6 Down, the lowest point

explanation.surface: An instruction to redo the answer to 6 Down.
explanation.walkthrough: '6 Down' reads as one cross-reference, but only the 6 points to the other answer; 'Down' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain a glass is to drink it all, which is what downing it means.

clue.text: Cheerful rejection of accusation good for Duke

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another, so the good letter replaces the duke's

parts.note: a denial is a refusal to admit a charge

explanation.surface: A duke cheerfully denies a charge made against him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone genial is friendly and good-humoured, so cheerful in manner.

clue.text: Flapper wearing delicate fabric for British colonel overseas

indicators.note: the bird is wrapped in the fabric, as though dressed in it

parts.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric
a wren flaps its wings, a bird as something that flaps

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper girl dressed in lace stands in for a British officer abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' suggests a jazz-age young woman, but it is a bird. T. E. Lawrence, 'Lawrence of Arabia', was a British army colonel in the Arab Revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: T. E. Lawrence served as a British colonel in the Middle East during the First World War.

clue.text: Tropical island's greeting inspired by French movie star

indicators.note: taken in by, as breath is inspired, so the greeting goes inside the actor's name

parts.note: Jacques Tati was the French comic actor and director of Monsieur Hulot films
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A tropical island's welcome was inspired by a French film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Mr Benn's overwhelming sex appeal leading to merriment

indicators.note: the name engulfs the short word, closing round it

parts.note: Hilary Benn is a Labour politician, son of Tony Benn
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A politician's overpowering allure ends in laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Benn' also calls to mind the children's cartoon character, but here it is Hilary Benn the MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is boisterous amusement and laughter, which is merriment.

clue.text: Live with a penniless revolutionary and eccentrics

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: revolving the word turns it round so it reads backwards

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money

explanation.surface: Living with a broke radical and other oddballs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for the radical, but it signals a reversal of SKINT, British slang for broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatniks were the 1950s bohemian nonconformists, so unconventional people or eccentrics.

clue.text: Director books in to get Oscar after so long

indicators.note: the books, in and Oscar all follow the farewell word

parts.note: ta-ra is a northern English way of saying goodbye
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A film director gets an Oscar at last after taking books in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' tempts as the Academy Award, apt for a director, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is the American film director of Pulp Fiction.

clue.text: It's bang out of order to support 500 idiots

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting letters sit beneath, so the numeral goes on top

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: the letters are put in a disordered sequence

explanation.surface: Backing five hundred fools is said to be completely unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingbats is informal slang for stupid or foolish people.

clue.text: Hypersensitive and intolerant Eurosceptics in charge after all!

indicators.note: the group and the charge letters come after the word all

parts.note: the ERG, European Research Group, is the Eurosceptic caucus of Conservative MPs

explanation.surface: Eurosceptics running the show turn out to be touchy and bigoted after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intolerant' reads as narrow-minded politics, but it is the medical sense, as in lactose intolerant.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergic person reacts badly to a substance, so their body is oversensitive to it and cannot tolerate it.

clue.text: Remains being supported by male in religious retreat

indicators.note: in a down answer the remains sit on top, held up by the male below

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Someone's ashes are carried by a man to a place of retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage or community for religious retreat.

clue.text: Advises cheese factories to be evacuated

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: the word is emptied of its inside, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone recommends clearing out the cheese plants.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to instruct or inform them in advance, so to advise.

clue.text: Panties off, which is wise

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking one's knickers off is the sensible thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a literary word for having great wisdom or discernment.

clue.text: Their fantastic maturity provides legacy

indicators.note: fantastic in the sense of fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: to come of age is to reach maturity

explanation.surface: A couple's wonderful wisdom is what they leave behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what is handed down from earlier generations, an inheritance or bequest.

clue.text: Body half of American politicians love

indicators.note: the word is halved and only its second four letters are kept

parts.note: senators sit in the US Senate
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Half the members of the US Congress are said to be in love.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Home kit rejected — it goes black then disintegrates

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pack is a set of kit or gear

explanation.surface: A football team's home strip is turned down for going black and falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Kit suggests a football strip, but it is a pack of gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The inkcap is a mushroom whose cap turns to black inky liquid as it decays.

clue.text: Rise of conservative member

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: The rise of a Tory member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an ascent, an upward movement, as a rise is.

clue.text: Sanction to stop church providing solid fuel

indicators.note: the approval plugs the church letters, as a stopper fills a gap

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to OK something is to approve or sanction it

explanation.surface: Approval to shut a church down supplies fuel for the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is a solid fuel made by heating coal to drive off its gases.

clue.text: Change harness covering head

indicators.note: the head of the word is covered over and so lost from view

parts.note: a halter is a rope harness for leading a horse

explanation.surface: Altering a harness that goes over a horse's head.
explanation.walkthrough: A halter is indeed a harness worn over an animal's head, so the surface reads as description before it gives up its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify or change it.

clue.text: Native of India entertained by American tennis legend in Spain

indicators.note: a guest is held inside by the host, so the letter sits within the name

parts.note: Björn Borg won Wimbledon five times running
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: An Indian native is hosted by an American tennis great in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native of India' reads as one phrase, but only 'Native' defines; India gives the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is an original inhabitant of a land, one of its indigenous people.

clue.text: Comrades both injured, unable to fight

indicators.note: the letters are damaged and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Two comrades are both wounded and out of the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hors de combat is a French phrase, now used in English, for out of action through injury.
